Decisions about hiring, credit, or medical care may not be made by an AI system alone. A trained employee must review and approve each high-risk recommendation.
Third-party AI vendors must pass a security and privacy assessment before contract signature. The assessment checks data retention, model training on customer data, and breach notification terms.
Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems may only index documents from approved repositories. Audio and video files must be transcribed by the approved speech recognition service before indexing.
Production language model applications must monitor for prompt injection attempts. Suspicious prompts are blocked, logged, and reported to the AI Governance Board every week.
The AI governance board keeps an inventory of every model and production. The inventory lists the model version, its owner, its training data source, and the date of the last audit.
Data used to train or fine-tune models must have a documented license. Personal data may only be used for training after a privacy review and approval from the data protection officer.
Harmful or incorrect outputs from an AI system must be reported as incidents. The model owner investigates the cause and may roll back to the previous model version.
Privileged accounts are reviewed every month by the account owner and the security team. Accounts that are no longer needed are disabled on the same day.
Access rights follow the principle of least privilege. Employees receive only the permissions their role requires, and temporary elevated access expires after eight hours.
passwords must contain at least 14 characters and may not appear in known breach lists. password managers are recommended and passwords are never sent by email.
When an employee leaves, all accounts and access badges are disabled on the last working day. Shared passwords The person you must be changed within 24 hours.
Service accounts may not be used for interactive login, their credentials are stored in the secret's vault and rotated automatically every 90 days.
Administrators and other privileged users must authenticate with a hardware security key. Lost keys are reported immediately and the account is locked until a new key is issued.
Requests for access to production systems need approval from the system owner. The approval, the reason, and the end date are recorded in the access management tool.
accounts are locked for 15 minutes after five failed login attempts. Repeated lockouts on a privileged account trigger an alert to the Security Operations Center.
All internal applications must use the company's single sign on service. Local application passwords are not allowed so that disabling one account removes all access.
Personal and confidential data must be encrypted in transit. File transfers use secure protocols and unencrypted email attachments containing customer data are blocked.
All data is classified as public, internal, confidential, or restricted. The data owner assigns the class and the class decides the required encryption and access rules.
Copying confidential data to USB drives or other removable media is not allowed. Exceptions require approval, and the device must be encrypted and registered.
Encryption keys for customer data are rotated every year, old keys are kept only to decrypt archive data, and every key operation is recorded in an audit log.
Teams may collect only the personal data needed for a stated purpose. Extra fields must be removed from forms and unused data is deleted during the yearly review.
Restore tests confirm that backups can recover a full database within four hours. Failed restore tests are treated as incidents and fixed before the next nightly backup.
